home.headline:
Build beautiful
desktop UIs in Python
home.subline: cs-ui packages Flet 1.0's declarative components, Material 3 theming, and a complete form toolkit into one composable UI language. Write Python, ship a native desktop experience.

cta.title: Ready to build?
cta.desc: From install to your first screen takes only a few minutes.

hero.point1: Pure Python, no frontend build step
hero.point2: Three languages, live switching · light & dark

features.title: Why cs-ui
features.hint: Let the library handle UI plumbing so you can focus on the product.

reactive.title: Declarative state
reactive.desc: @ft.component and hooks drive the UI. State changes repaint automatically—no manual update calls.

themed.title: Material 3 theming
themed.desc: One seed color derives the entire palette. Dark mode and semantic colors work out of the box.

i18n.title: Runtime i18n
i18n.desc: Switch between Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, and English live—dates and numbers follow.

typed.title: Fully typed
typed.desc: Built for Python 3.12+ with signatures on every public API, so editor completion stays reliable.

modular.title: Composable
modular.desc: Layout, forms, feedback, and charts share one set of design tokens and stay consistent together.

desktop.title: Desktop first
desktop.desc: Designed for mouse and keyboard: hover states, density, scrolling, and window sizing all considered.

catalog.title: Browse by category
catalog.hint: Nine categories cover the vast majority of everyday desktop UI needs.

playground.title: Try it
playground.hint: These are real components. Switching language or theme keeps your input intact.

why.title: Less glue code, more product
why.desc: cs-ui concentrates routing, theming, language, and form state into a few entry points, so page code only describes what the UI looks like.
why.point1: Root-view rendering keeps overlays and dialogs out of the view stack
why.point2: Theme and locale are subscribable state, repainting only what changed
why.point3: Stateful components keep user input when the language changes
why.point4: Shared design tokens end the per-page spacing guessing game

requirements.title: Requirements
requirements.desc: cs-ui targets modern Python desktop development with a deliberately small dependency set.
requirements.note: Use Python 3.12 or newer and stay on the Flet 1.0.x line.
requirements.python: Python 3.12+ using the latest typing syntax
requirements.flet: Flet 1.0.5 with declarative components and hooks
requirements.deps: A small set of third-party packages such as flet-code-editor

install.title: Install
install.desc: Pick whichever fits your workflow and keep Flet in sync with cs-ui when upgrading.

quickstart.title: Your first screen
quickstart.desc: Create main.py and render a minimal app with theming and a card.

run.title: Run
run.desc: Turn on hot reload during development and the UI refreshes as you edit.

project.title: Suggested project layout
project.desc: Keep pages, business components, catalogs, and assets separate as the app grows.

next.title: Next steps
next.desc: Learn how routing, providers, and stateful components fit together.

overview.title: Layered overview
overview.desc: cs-ui adds four layers on top of Flet: controls, state, infrastructure, and application composition.
points: Controls: styled wrappers around native Flet controls, ready to construct.
State: @ft.observable data objects with a ui() rendering method.
Infrastructure: theme, locale, routing, formatting, and design tokens.
Application: page components compose; they don't touch the plumbing.

paradigm.title: Two kinds of components
paradigm.desc: Static controls subclass Flet controls directly; interactive components use observable data objects.
paradigm.note: Stateful components must be constructed inside @ft.component and pinned with a ref, or every parent re-render recreates the object and loses input.

providers.title: Provider order
providers.desc: Locale outermost, theme next, router innermost. The order decides first-frame colors and copy.

routing.title: Declarative routing
routing.desc: Render into the root view with manage_views=False so overlays, dialogs, and dropdown panels keep working.
routing.note: render_views creates a view stack that covers the page overlay. Dialogs and hanging panels fail silently.

state.title: State management
state.desc: Use hooks for local state and module-level observable singletons for cross-page state.
points: use_state manages state inside a component.
use_ref pins an instance across renders.
use_memo caches expensive computation.
Subscribed module-level state powers global theme and locale.

performance.title: Performance stance
performance.desc: Rendering repaints at subscription granularity; changing theme or language doesn't rebuild the tree.
points: Only components that read use_t() or use_theme() repaint.
Route changes keep the layout shell mounted.
Code blocks and charts are built on demand to keep the first frame light.
Form instances are reused instead of recreated on every keystroke.

live.title: Live theming
live.hint: Switch mode or accent color and the whole site updates instantly—without losing form input.

preview.title: Preview panel
preview.body: Panels, text, and buttons all use Material 3 role colors, so contrast holds in both light and dark mode.

semantic.title: Semantic colors
semantic.desc: success, warning, danger, info, and neutral are decoupled from the palette and stay readable in either mode.

tokens.title: Design tokens
tokens.desc: Spacing, radius, type scale, and elevation all come from ui—no magic numbers.

modes.title: Light and dark
modes.desc: ThemeProvider writes page.theme and exposes subscribable state.
points: mode: system, light, or dark.
primary: the seed color behind the whole palette.
font_family: the global font family.
Subscribe with use_theme() and repaint on change.

trap.title: Don't set page.theme from a page
trap.desc: Page components run one frame late, so direct changes flash the old palette. Go through ThemeProvider and use_theme() instead.

live.title: Switch language live
live.hint: Page copy, dates, and number formats all update the moment you switch.

overview.title: One runtime
overview.desc: Copy lives outside the code. Switching language needs no restart and no router rebuild.
points: Three JSON catalogs load once at startup.
use_t() is the only subscription point; only subscribed components repaint.
Framework-owned copy (pagers, calendars) follows automatically.
The chosen locale is persisted locally.

register.title: Register messages
register.desc: Register nested dictionaries with register_messages; keys resolve with dot notation.
register.note: Traditional Chinese falls back to Simplified, then English. No step ever yields a blank string or a raw key.

use.title: Use it in a component
use.desc: Call use_t() at the top of the component body, then read copy with tr(key, **params).

format.title: Formatting
format.desc: Dates, numbers, and calendar titles all follow the active locale.
points: format_number adds thousands separators.
format_date supports short and long forms.
calendar_title produces a localized month heading.
English switches date order to month/day/year automatically.

fallback.title: Fallback strategy
fallback.desc: A catalog can be partially translated; the rest resolves through the chain.
points: zh_TW → zh_CN → en_US.
Missing keys never raise.
Untranslated keys surface in development logs.

persist.title: Persistence
persist.desc: Desktop builds write the choice to a local JSON file and restore it on launch; swap in a custom LocaleStore if needed.
